info.name: Movie Reservation System — Full API
info.description: End-to-end manual-testing collection for every implemented endpoint (docs/api/README.md). Designed to be run top-to-bottom via Collection Runner: each run registers a fresh throwaway customer and creates its own genre/movie/showtime, chains their ids through collection variables, and tears everything down in the final Cleanup folder — so it is safe to re-run repeatedly without manual reset. To run a single folder by hand, run Auth first (it seeds the tokens/ids every later request depends on).

request.description: Captures customerUserId — the id is not in the register/login response, only here.
ADR-005: rotation — the old refreshToken is now revoked, so this test script overwrites the stored variable with the new pair.
Kept for the rest of the run — used by 'Create movie'. See 'Create spare genre' for the delete demo.
Never attached to a movie, so Cleanup can DELETE it without hitting 409 GENRE_IN_USE — demonstrates a clean genre delete.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "{{movieTitle}}",
  "synopsis": "A movie created by the Postman collection.",
  "durationMinutes": 120,
  "language": "en",
  "releaseDate": "2026-01-01",
  "rating": 7.5,
  "genreIds": ["{{genreId}}"]
}

exec: pm.test('has at least one hall (seed data)', () => pm.expect(body.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Halls are read-only (DDR-015) — captures hallId from the seeded halls for use by 'Create showtime'.

exec: // Varies both the day and the time-of-day by run so re-running the
// whole collection (e.g. Collection Runner, back to back) doesn't
// collide with a showtime a previous run already created in the
// same hall — (hallId, showDate, showTime) is unique (BR-16).

request.description: 30–329 days out at a randomized time to avoid colliding with seed data or a previous run's throwaway showtime in the same hall — a 409 SHOWTIME_OVERLAP here means an actual collision, just re-run.
Bearer is optional here (just flags isMine) — sent as the customer since that's who holds the seat next.
Only legal while status is still 'scheduled' (409 SHOWTIME_NOT_MODIFIABLE otherwise).
10-minute hold (DDR-001) — confirm the reservation in the next request before it expires.

item.name: Hold second seat, for the release demo (customer)

request.description: A second, disposable hold — kept separate from {{holdId}} so releasing it below does not disturb the seat that Confirm reservation needs later.
The caller's active (held, not-yet-expired) holds across all showtimes — what a resumed checkout screen fetches to know what's already selected.
Voluntary HELD → RELEASED on the second hold above — frees the seat immediately instead of waiting out the 10-minute TTL.
DDR-002 confirmation transaction — HELD seat hold becomes CONFIRMED, a ticket is issued.
Proves the owner-or-admin rule: an admin token can read a reservation it does not own.
Run against the throwaway customer, never the admin — safe to re-run since customerPassword is updated after and a fresh customer is registered next run.
Deliberately a no-op body (isActive is already true) so it doesn't disturb the rest of the run — edit the body to try role/isActive changes by hand.
Revokes the refresh token. The deactivated customer's accessToken stays valid until it expires, per this design's stateless-access-token model.
